newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin says Russia's economic decline has halted.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin says Russia's economic decline has halted.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin told the Russian people on Friday that the past year had been the hardest of his life but industrial decline had now been halted and the economy could start growing.

"The breakthrough has already happened," Yeltsin said in a radio address marking the anniversary of his re-election for a second presidential term. "That is it. We have reached the point when it is possible for production to go up. The decline has been stopped."
Yeltsin, speaking clearly and fluently, gave no figures and did not say when or by how much the economy would grow. It would take time for the Russian people to feel the benefit, he added.

"In 1995 and 1996 we could not even dream of this," he said. "In individual regions there is already a small growth. True, it is still small. People will be able to feel the growth when it starts in the majority of regions."

Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin said on Wednesday the economy had already started growing. He said gross domestic product, the broadest measure of economic health, had risen one percent in the first six months of this year.
It was the first rise in GDP, the total value of goods and services produced, since the Soviet Union collapsed in 1991.
Yeltsin, 66, defeated a communist challenger against the odds to secure a four-year second term last July.
He spent most of the first eight months of his new term out of the Kremlin because of health problems, but has reaffirmed his grip on power since undergoing heart surgery last November.

"This year, I think, was the most difficult of my life, but it was also a special, unique one. I could never have imagined that a man of my age could change so much. But that is how it turned out. I can feel how I have changed," he said.
As one of the major changes, Yeltsin cited a newly acquired ability to seek and find compromise with opponents, including the communist-dominated State Duma lower house of parliament.
Yeltsin praised the government for managing to pay off huge pension arrears, fulfilling an order he gave them last December.
The next task, he said, was to ensure months of wage arrears are settled with the armed forces and other public sector workers such as doctors and teachers.
